root_idea.summary: The root centers on advancing or moving forward slowly, heavily, or with a dragging motion.
root_idea.development: Its usages extend from a child crawling and a fatigued animal dragging its foot to a massed army advancing toward an enemy; related branches describe sliding, slow movement, and reciprocal approach in combat.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The sole Quran-attested group is a nominal use with an independently supported military-advance sense.

senses.definition: A massed military advance toward the enemy; a force moving slowly or heavily as it closes with the opposing side.
senses.usage_conditions: In 8:15, زَحْفًا is an accusative adverbial use describing a group or military force advancing. The noun denotes a massed force or collective advance, not a single individual.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To walk, march, or move slowly, gently, or heavily, sometimes by creeping; also, of young locusts, to proceed onward.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form I verb used of people, groups, or creatures; the slow onward movement of young locusts is a specialized application.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a child, to crawl or drag himself along the ground, on the buttocks or belly, before walking.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specific construction describing a child’s pre-walking movement.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of an arrow that falls short of the target, to slide along the ground until reaching it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized usage said of an arrow’s movement after falling short.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a walker, beast, or especially a camel, to become fatigued while walking or marching, dragging the foot or its extremity and sometimes standing still with its owner.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The usage may apply to a person or beast; the camel-specific construction emphasizes fatigue and dragging the foot.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For trees to move gently under the influence of the wind; for the wind to put trees into such gentle motion.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative or tropical usage describing wind-driven movement of trees.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To drag a thing along gently.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A transitive Form I construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To sweep a house or chamber with a زَحَّافَة.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form II construction taking the house or chamber as its object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An implement, commonly a palm branch, used to sweep dust and cobwebs from the roof and walls of a house or chamber.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An Egyptian dialect noun; the implement is also used in the Form II sweeping construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To fight with someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form III reciprocal or interactional construction, attested in the expression زَاحَفُونَا, “they fought with us.”

other_classical_meanings.definition: Said of a man, for his camel, horse, or similar mount to become fatigued; a long journey fatigued the camels.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form IV construction in which the subject is associated with the fatigued mount or with the journey causing the fatigue.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For a group to become a زَحْفٌ—an army marching toward others to fight them.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form IV construction describing the formation or approach of a military force.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To attain the utmost of what one sought or desired.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An independently attested Form IV idiomatic usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To draw near to one another in combat; to walk or march toward one another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form VI reciprocal construction, especially used of opposing parties approaching for a fight.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A swarm of locusts.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative noun use likening the collective movement of locusts to a creeping or advancing mass.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In فَرَّ مِنَ الزَّحْفِ, the battle with unbelievers or the encounter with the enemy.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional expression referring to fleeing from battle.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A walk or instance of creeping, slow movement, or advance.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A nominal of instance or occurrence derived from the movement sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A rapidly blazing fire from which people move away, then return when it subsides.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional expression named for the repeated movement away from and back to the fire.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A man who does not travel about in the countries.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized nominal description of a sedentary or non-wandering person.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Going along slowly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An independently attested descriptive usage; the related entry also cross-references the active-participial branch.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person who creeps along on the ground because of fatigue or old age.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized noun describing a person unable or barely able to walk normally.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A man whose heel-tendons nearly strike against one another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An anatomical descriptive usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An arrow that falls short of the target and then slides along to it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A nominal active-participial use applied to the arrow.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Fatigued and dragging the foot or its extremity; of a camel, fatigued and possibly standing still with its owner.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An active-participial description applied to a male or female animal and, more generally, to something fatigued and motionless.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of clouds, moving slowly because they carry much water.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative participial usage likening heavily laden clouds to fatigued camels.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A place where serpents creep, or the mark or track left by a serpent on the ground.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A place-noun and track sense, also used of the visible trail of a serpent.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The places where a party or people fight.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A plural place-noun usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The places where cloud-water is poured or where rain from the clouds falls.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative place-noun usage referring to rainfall locations.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A camel accustomed to becoming fatigued, dragging its foot, or standing still with its owner; figuratively, a she-camel that quickly becomes attenuated or worn in the sole of the foot.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized noun for a fatigue-prone camel, with a further feminine and figurative application concerning wear of the foot sole.
